newsitem.title: CHINA: China central bank keeps yuan/dlr below 8.2900.
newsitem.headline: China central bank keeps yuan/dlr below 8.2900.

text.p: The Chinese yuan failed to convincingly breach the key resistance level of 8.2900 to the dollar again on Thursday and it ended slightly lower amid fairly strong central bank intervention, dealers said.
They said central bank intervention to halt an advance prompted speculative selling of the local unit which ended at 8.2903 against its 8.2900 close on Wednesday.
The weighted average price on Thursday was 8.2901.
However, the yuan briefly tested a new high of 8.2876 -- after reaching an intraday high of 8.2899 on Wednesday -- and that showed sentiment toward the yuan remained bullish, dealers said.
The yuan opened unchanged at 8.2900 and mainly traded around 8.2902, hitting an intraday low of 8.2905.
"The People's Bank of China was seen pressuring the yuan at the 8.2900 level for nearly the entire trading session," one dealer said.
"The intervention kept the yuan from breaching that level though buying was active at low levels," he said.
Another dealer said the currency would not be allowed to breach the key level with any conviction, and that could eventually change sentiment toward the local unit.
"If that key level cannot be breached in the near term, the bullish yuan sentiment could be hurt slightly," he added.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to hold near the 8.2900 level on Friday.
The yuan closed down at 7.0100 from 7.0083 against 100 Japanese yen and little changed at 1.0695 from 1.0696 against the Hong Kong dollar.
